title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 7
statement: A charity sells \(140\) benefit tickets for a total of \(\$2001.\) Some tickets sell for full price (a whole dollar amount), and the rest sell for half price. How much money is raised by the full-price tickets?

solutions.text:
Let \(n\) tickets sell at full price \(p\) dollars. Then \[ np + (140 - n)\dfrac{p}{2} = 2001, \] so \(p(n + 140)\) \(= 4002\) \(= 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 23 \cdot 29.\)

Since \(0 \le n \le 140,\) we need a factor of \(4002\) with \(140 \le n + 140 \le 280.\) The only such factor is \(174 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 29,\) giving \(n = 34\) and \(p = 23.\)

The full-price tickets raise \(34 \cdot 23 = 782\) dollars.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: With \(n\) full-price tickets at price \(p,\) the total is \(np + (140 - n)\dfrac{p}{2} = 2001\)
This becomes \(p(n + 140)\) \(= 4002\) \(= 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 23 \cdot 29,\) and \(n + 140\) lies between \(140\) and \(280\)
